newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta call money stable, bond prices on uptrend.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta call money stable, bond prices on uptrend.

text.p: Jakarta call money was stable at 14.0/14.5 percent on Monday morning on sufficient liquidity.
Bond dealers said bond prices continued to rise on sustained demand, keeping pressure on the average yields.
One foreign bank dealer said there was still carry-forward impact from last Friday when overnight money was fluctuating.
On Monday, longer-term rates indicated some uptrend, with one- and three-month money quoted at 12.75/13.00 and 13.25/13.50 percent, respectively.
Dealers said operators were also getting cautious with the approaching festivities of the lunar New Year on February 7 and the Eid al-Fitr on February 9 and 10.
They said sustained capital inflows in the capital market might keep further pressure on interest rates.
Stock dealers said the stock market composite index was rising to a high of 670.35 in mid-morning, the highest level since 1990 when the index hit 681.94.
The central bank had also cut another 25 basis points for longer-term bilateral papers (SBIs) last Friday, indicating a further move to curb offshore inflows in longer-term papers.

The central bank offered 1-3 day SBIs at seven percent, 4-7 day at eight percent, 8-11 day at 9.5 percent, 14-18 day at 10.5 percent, one-month at 11.5 percent, three-, six- and 12-month money to 12.25, 12.50 and 12.75 percent.
Bond dealers said prices for selective bonds rose between 25 and 100 basis points on Monday morning, putting average yield at around 15.5 to 16.0 percent.
The average overnight interbank rate on Friday was 21.52 percent against 7.7 percent on Thursday.
